title: Counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS)
description: CEGIS splits synthesis into two agents: a synthesizer proposes a program from examples, and a verifier checks it against the full specification. When verification fails, the counterexample becomes a new example and the loop repeats. The Sketch system pioneered this: programs are synthesized to satisfy assertions, with the verifier driving convergence.
method: Synthesize candidate from examples -> verify against spec -> on failure, add counterexample to examples -> repeat until verified or timeout.
usage: Write a precise spec first — CEGIS is only as good as the verifier checking the candidates.

demo.code:
examples = [(2, 4), (3, 9)]
print('CEGIS loop: synth proposes f(x)=x+x from', examples)
print('verifier counterexample: f(3)=6 != 9 -> add (3,9)')
print('synth proposes f(x)=x*x -> verifier: PROVED')

title: Proof-carrying synthesized code
description: Proof-carrying code attaches a machine-checkable proof to the program: the synthesizer must produce both code and evidence it meets the spec. The consumer checks the proof in milliseconds without trusting the synthesizer — verification is decoupled from (possibly untrusted) synthesis.
method: Synthesizer emits (program, proof); a small trusted checker validates the proof against the spec; only proof-valid programs execute.
usage: Use for untrusted synthesis sources (third-party agents, marketplaces of generated code).

demo.code:
prog, proof = 'sort(xs)', 'proof: permutation + ordered (checked)'
print('program:', prog)
print('checker verdict:', 'VALID' if 'checked' in proof else 'REJECT')

title: Contract-driven agent code review
description: Every function the agent writes carries contracts (preconditions, postconditions, invariants). A review agent checks each contract with symbolic execution or testing before merge — the codebase accumulates machine-checked documentation as agents write.
method: Agent emits code + contracts; reviewer runs contract checks (runtime assertion testing + static checks); violations return to the author agent with the failing contract.
usage: Require contracts on all agent-authored functions; make the reviewer a merge gate.

demo.code:
print('contract check:')
print('  pre:  x >= 0')
print('  post: result*result <= x < (result+1)*(result+1)')
print('  500 random tests: all contracts hold -> MERGE')

title: Verified lifting of legacy code
description: Verified lifting translates legacy code (say, C loops) into a high-level DSL (say, Halide schedules) and proves equivalence. The synthesis agent searches the DSL space; an SMT solver proves the lifted program matches the original on all inputs — modernization with a correctness proof.
method: Parse legacy code; search DSL programs via synthesis; prove equivalence with an SMT solver; replace only on proof success.
usage: Target hot loops for DSL/accelerator ports; require the equivalence proof before swapping implementations.

demo.code:
print('lifting C loop -> Halide:')
print('  synthesized schedule found; Z3 proves equiv on all inputs')
print('  swap approved: 14x faster, provably identical')

title: Differential verification against reference
description: When a reference implementation exists, the verifier proves the synthesized version agrees with it on all inputs (bounded or unbounded) instead of proving an abstract spec. Differential verification is often easier than full specification — correctness means 'same as the trusted original'.
method: Encode both programs symbolically; ask the solver for an input where outputs differ; UNSAT means equivalent.
usage: Keep a trusted reference (even a slow one); verify optimized syntheses against it automatically.

demo.code:
print('differential check: ref vs synthesized on 10,000 random inputs')
print('  mismatches: 0 -> EQUIVALENT (bounded proof)')

title: Synthesis repair from failed proofs
description: When verification of human-written code fails, the failed proof pinpoints the broken region; a synthesis agent then searches for a local fix that makes the proof go through. Failed verification becomes a repair work order with the proof obligation as the spec.
method: Run verifier; extract the unprovable subgoal; synthesize a replacement for the implicated code region; re-verify; iterate.
usage: Wire the repair agent to CI: red proofs automatically get repair attempts before human triage.

demo.code:
print('proof failed at: loop invariant too weak')
print('synth proposes stronger invariant: 0 <= i <= n')
print('re-verify: PROVED -> auto-repair merged')

title: SyGuS syntax-guided synthesis
description: Syntax-Guided Synthesis (SyGuS) constrains the synthesizer to a grammar of allowed constructs plus a semantic spec. The grammar keeps generated code idiomatic and reviewable (no bizarre but 'correct' programs), while the spec guarantees behavior — synthesis with style control.
method: Provide grammar G and spec phi; the solver searches L(G) for a program satisfying phi; standard SyGuS-IF format for tool interop.
usage: Write the grammar to match your codebase idioms; the synthesized code will look like it belongs.

demo.code:
print('SyGuS: grammar allows {+, -, *, if}; spec: f(x) = |x|')
print('synthesized: (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x)  -- idiomatic, verified')

title: Sketch-based program sketching
description: In sketching, the human writes a program with holes (unknown constants, unknown expressions) and the synthesizer fills them to satisfy assertions. It splits the work sensibly: humans provide structure and insight, the machine searches the combinatorial details.
method: Write sketch with ?? holes; encode as SAT/SMT constraints with assertions; solve; substitute the solution back into the sketch.
usage: Sketch the algorithm shape; assert the required behavior; let the solver fill constants and bit-twiddling.

demo.code:
print('sketch: int f(int x) { return x * ??; }')
print('assert f(3) == 21; assert f(4) == 28;')
print('solver fills ?? = 7 -> verified program')
